learning_outcomes.text: Possess the ability to design, develop, implement, manage and improve products, systems and processes in different industrial areas, using appropriate analytical, computational or experimental techniques.
Apply acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess the learning skills that allow continuous lifelong learning for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools in their professional activities.
Organization and planning of projects and human teams. Teamwork and leadership ability.
Use of the English language at written and oral level.
Knowledge and capacities to understand the management and functioning of organizations in general and production companies in particular.

syllabus_topics: History and theories of Industrial Organization.
Strategic Planning. Types of business strategies.
Cost Accounting and Strategic Management Accounting.
Break-even point or Profitability Threshold. Operating Leverage.
ABC cost system in Analytical Accounting.
Sustainability Reports. ESG indicators (environmental, social, and governance).
Supply chain management and its risks.
Selection of goods and services: their life cycle and competitive advantage.
Organization for product development and design.
Design for manufacturing and value engineering.
Robust, modular, computer-aided design, value analysis and ethical and ecological design.
Technology acquisition, alliances and joint ventures.
Product documents: engineering drawings and bill of materials.
Manufacture or outsource components, or services.
Assembly drawing, assembly diagram, route sheet, work order, engineering change notices and configuration management.
Application of decision trees to product design.
Process Strategy, Automation and Capacity Planning.
Productive configuration strategies: process, repetitive, product and mass customization.
Flow diagrams, time-function maps, process chart and service process design.
Selection of equipment and technology. Types of automation.
Actual, projected capacity. Utilization and efficiency of designed capacity.
Break-even analysis and operating leverage in capacity planning.
Methods for evaluating location alternatives: weighted factors, break-even, center of gravity and transport model.
Types of plant layout: fixed position, process and product.
Quality and Strategy. From quality inspection to TQM.
Human resources management processes: recruitment, selection, training, career development, evaluation, remuneration and dismissal.
Job design: specialization, rotation, enrichment, diversification, teamwork.
Motivation and incentives. Theories of Taylor, Maslow and Herzberg.
Aggregate Planning and Master Production Schedule.
Aggregate planning strategies: supply, demand, pure, mixed.
Planning methods: tables and graphs, transportation, linear programming, coefficients, Gantt and PERT.
Inventory management: ABC analysis, cycle counting, accuracy.
Inventory management models: independent demand versus dependent demand.
Requirements for planning independent demand models such as MRP.
MRP structure. Net material requirements planning.
Extensions of MRP I: MRP II, ERP, DRP SCM, CRM.
What is JIT? Its strategic advantages.
Maintenance strategy: types, costs and implementation.
assessment_rules: For progressive evaluation, two written exams (40% each) and two group assignments (10% each) are graded. A minimum of 4/10 is required on each exam, and an overall average of 5/10 is needed to pass. For ordinary and extraordinary calls, a single 100% written exam is administered, comprising theoretical-practical questions, problems, and a real case. If a student takes the Final Global Exam after passing by progressive evaluation, the final grade will be that of the Final Global Exam. Incorrect answers on multiple-choice items deduct half their value, with a minimum score of zero per question.
